pages.title: Shield System
pages.text: Before shield systems, every incoming attack had to be absorbed by armor. Even the strongest vessel suffered constant armor damage and required frequent repairs.$(br2)AeroIE shields now protect a vessel at little cost beyond the required energy.$(br2)An AeroIE shield is not a single component. Multiple Shield Generators work together to protect a spherical region centered on the subspace.

pages.title: Shield System: Construction
pages.text: Shield Generators are Control Seat peripherals, and any number may be linked to a seat on the same subspace. However, interference between generators changes the final shield performance. Use a Shield Tool to inspect the result; see $(l:vsie:shield/shield_tool)Shields: Shield Tool/$.$(br2)The formulas are listed in the next chapter and in the Shield Tool GUI.

pages.title: Shield System: Operation
pages.text: After linking Shield Generators to a Control Seat, press V to activate the shield. It draws energy from linked batteries until fully charged. Press V again to disable it; all Shield Generators are drained to zero and stop drawing power.$(br2)An active shield automatically spends energy to remove projectiles that enter its radius while traveling toward the Control Seat's subspace. Every linked generator consumes one share of energy for each intercepted projectile.

pages.title: Shield System: Overload
pages.text: When shield energy reaches zero, the system enters cooldown and cannot begin recharging until the cooldown ends.$(br2)For exact values, see the next chapter: $(l:vsie:shield/shield_generator_data)Shields: Parameter Formulas/$.
